work.title: The Tragedy of Romeo and Juliet
work.author: William Shakespeare

content.text: Enter Romeo, Mercutio, Benvolio, with five or six Maskers; Torch-bearers and others.

lines.text: What, shall this speech be spoke for our excuse?
lines.plainText: What shall this speech be spoke for our excuse

lines.text: Or shall we on without apology?
lines.plainText: Or shall we on without apology

lines.text: The date is out of such prolixity:
lines.plainText: The date is out of such prolixity

lines.text: We'll have no Cupid hoodwink'd with a scarf,
lines.plainText: We'll have no Cupid hoodwink'd with a scarf

lines.text: Bearing a Tartar's painted bow of lath,
lines.plainText: Bearing a Tartar's painted bow of lath

lines.text: Scaring the ladies like a crow-keeper;
lines.plainText: Scaring the ladies like a crowkeeper

lines.text: Nor no without-book prologue, faintly spoke
lines.plainText: Nor no withoutbook prologue faintly spoke

lines.text: After the prompter, for our entrance:
lines.plainText: After the prompter for our entrance

lines.text: But let them measure us by what they will,
lines.plainText: But let them measure us by what they will

lines.text: We'll measure them a measure, and be gone.
lines.plainText: We'll measure them a measure and be gone

lines.text: Give me a torch, I am not for this ambling;
lines.plainText: Give me a torch I am not for this ambling

lines.text: Being but heavy I will bear the light.
lines.plainText: Being but heavy I will bear the light

lines.text: Nay, gentle Romeo, we must have you dance.
lines.plainText: Nay gentle Romeo we must have you dance

lines.text: Not I, believe me, you have dancing shoes,
lines.plainText: Not I believe me you have dancing shoes

lines.text: With nimble soles, I have a soul of lead
lines.plainText: With nimble soles I have a soul of lead

lines.text: So stakes me to the ground I cannot move.
lines.plainText: So stakes me to the ground I cannot move

lines.text: You are a lover, borrow Cupid's wings,
lines.plainText: You are a lover borrow Cupid's wings

lines.text: And soar with them above a common bound.
lines.plainText: And soar with them above a common bound

lines.text: I am too sore enpierced with his shaft
lines.plainText: I am too sore enpierced with his shaft

lines.text: To soar with his light feathers, and so bound,
lines.plainText: To soar with his light feathers and so bound

lines.text: I cannot bound a pitch above dull woe.
lines.plainText: I cannot bound a pitch above dull woe

lines.text: Under love's heavy burden do I sink.
lines.plainText: Under love's heavy burden do I sink

lines.text: And, to sink in it, should you burden love;
lines.plainText: And to sink in it should you burden love

lines.text: Too great oppression for a tender thing.
lines.plainText: Too great oppression for a tender thing

lines.text: Is love a tender thing? It is too rough,
lines.plainText: Is love a tender thing It is too rough

lines.text: Too rude, too boisterous; and it pricks like thorn.
lines.plainText: Too rude too boisterous and it pricks like thorn

lines.text: If love be rough with you, be rough with love;
lines.plainText: If love be rough with you be rough with love

lines.text: Prick love for pricking, and you beat love down.
lines.plainText: Prick love for pricking and you beat love down

lines.text: Give me a case to put my visage in: [Putting on a mask.]
lines.plainText: Give me a case to put my visage in Putting on a mask

lines.text: A visor for a visor. What care I
lines.plainText: A visor for a visor What care I

lines.text: What curious eye doth quote deformities?
lines.plainText: What curious eye doth quote deformities

lines.text: Here are the beetle-brows shall blush for me.
lines.plainText: Here are the beetlebrows shall blush for me

lines.text: Come, knock and enter; and no sooner in
lines.plainText: Come knock and enter and no sooner in

lines.text: But every man betake him to his legs.
lines.plainText: But every man betake him to his legs

lines.text: A torch for me: let wantons, light of heart,
lines.plainText: A torch for me let wantons light of heart

lines.text: Tickle the senseless rushes with their heels;
lines.plainText: Tickle the senseless rushes with their heels

lines.text: For I am proverb'd with a grandsire phrase,
lines.plainText: For I am proverb'd with a grandsire phrase

lines.text: I'll be a candle-holder and look on,
lines.plainText: I'll be a candleholder and look on

lines.text: The game was ne'er so fair, and I am done.
lines.plainText: The game was ne'er so fair and I am done

lines.text: Tut, dun's the mouse, the constable's own word:
lines.plainText: Tut dun's the mouse the constable's own word

lines.text: If thou art dun, we'll draw thee from the mire
lines.plainText: If thou art dun we'll draw thee from the mire

lines.text: Or save your reverence love, wherein thou stickest
lines.plainText: Or save your reverence love wherein thou stickest

lines.text: Up to the ears. Come, we burn daylight, ho.
lines.plainText: Up to the ears Come we burn daylight ho

lines.text: Nay, that's not so.
lines.plainText: Nay that's not so

lines.text: I mean sir, in delay
lines.plainText: I mean sir in delay

lines.text: We waste our lights in vain, light lights by day.
lines.plainText: We waste our lights in vain light lights by day

lines.text: Take our good meaning, for our judgment sits
lines.plainText: Take our good meaning for our judgment sits

lines.text: Five times in that ere once in our five wits.
lines.plainText: Five times in that ere once in our five wits

lines.text: And we mean well in going to this mask;
lines.plainText: And we mean well in going to this mask

lines.text: But 'tis no wit to go.
lines.plainText: But 'tis no wit to go

lines.text: Why, may one ask?
lines.plainText: Why may one ask

lines.text: I dreamt a dream tonight.
lines.plainText: I dreamt a dream tonight

lines.text: And so did I.
lines.plainText: And so did I

lines.text: Well what was yours?
lines.plainText: Well what was yours

lines.text: That dreamers often lie.
lines.plainText: That dreamers often lie

lines.text: In bed asleep, while they do dream things true.
lines.plainText: In bed asleep while they do dream things true

lines.text: O, then, I see Queen Mab hath been with you.
lines.plainText: O then I see Queen Mab hath been with you

lines.text: She is the fairies' midwife, and she comes
lines.plainText: She is the fairies' midwife and she comes

lines.text: In shape no bigger than an agate-stone
lines.plainText: In shape no bigger than an agatestone

lines.text: On the fore-finger of an alderman,
lines.plainText: On the forefinger of an alderman

lines.text: Drawn with a team of little atomies
lines.plainText: Drawn with a team of little atomies

lines.text: Over men's noses as they lie asleep:
lines.plainText: Over men's noses as they lie asleep

lines.text: Her waggon-spokes made of long spinners' legs;
lines.plainText: Her waggonspokes made of long spinners' legs

lines.text: The cover, of the wings of grasshoppers;
lines.plainText: The cover of the wings of grasshoppers

lines.text: Her traces, of the smallest spider's web;
lines.plainText: Her traces of the smallest spider's web

lines.text: The collars, of the moonshine's watery beams;
lines.plainText: The collars of the moonshine's watery beams

lines.text: Her whip of cricket's bone; the lash, of film;
lines.plainText: Her whip of cricket's bone the lash of film

lines.text: Her waggoner, a small grey-coated gnat,
lines.plainText: Her waggoner a small greycoated gnat

lines.text: Not half so big as a round little worm
lines.plainText: Not half so big as a round little worm

lines.text: Prick'd from the lazy finger of a maid:
lines.plainText: Prick'd from the lazy finger of a maid

lines.text: Her chariot is an empty hazelnut,
lines.plainText: Her chariot is an empty hazelnut

lines.text: Made by the joiner squirrel or old grub,
lines.plainText: Made by the joiner squirrel or old grub

lines.text: Time out o' mind the fairies' coachmakers.
lines.plainText: Time out o' mind the fairies' coachmakers

lines.text: And in this state she gallops night by night
lines.plainText: And in this state she gallops night by night

lines.text: Through lovers' brains, and then they dream of love;
lines.plainText: Through lovers' brains and then they dream of love

lines.text: O'er courtiers' knees, that dream on curtsies straight;
lines.plainText: O'er courtiers' knees that dream on curtsies straight

lines.text: O'er lawyers' fingers, who straight dream on fees;
lines.plainText: O'er lawyers' fingers who straight dream on fees

lines.text: O'er ladies' lips, who straight on kisses dream,
lines.plainText: O'er ladies' lips who straight on kisses dream

lines.text: Which oft the angry Mab with blisters plagues,
lines.plainText: Which oft the angry Mab with blisters plagues

lines.text: Because their breaths with sweetmeats tainted are:
lines.plainText: Because their breaths with sweetmeats tainted are

lines.text: Sometime she gallops o'er a courtier's nose,
lines.plainText: Sometime she gallops o'er a courtier's nose

lines.text: And then dreams he of smelling out a suit;
lines.plainText: And then dreams he of smelling out a suit

lines.text: And sometime comes she with a tithe-pig's tail,
lines.plainText: And sometime comes she with a tithepig's tail

lines.text: Tickling a parson's nose as a lies asleep,
lines.plainText: Tickling a parson's nose as a lies asleep

lines.text: Then dreams he of another benefice:
lines.plainText: Then dreams he of another benefice

lines.text: Sometime she driveth o'er a soldier's neck,
lines.plainText: Sometime she driveth o'er a soldier's neck

lines.text: And then dreams he of cutting foreign throats,
lines.plainText: And then dreams he of cutting foreign throats

lines.text: Of breaches, ambuscados, Spanish blades,
lines.plainText: Of breaches ambuscados Spanish blades

lines.text: Of healths five fathom deep; and then anon
lines.plainText: Of healths five fathom deep and then anon

lines.text: Drums in his ear, at which he starts and wakes;
lines.plainText: Drums in his ear at which he starts and wakes

lines.text: And, being thus frighted, swears a prayer or two,
lines.plainText: And being thus frighted swears a prayer or two

lines.text: And sleeps again. This is that very Mab
lines.plainText: And sleeps again This is that very Mab

lines.text: That plats the manes of horses in the night;
lines.plainText: That plats the manes of horses in the night

lines.text: And bakes the elf-locks in foul sluttish hairs,
lines.plainText: And bakes the elflocks in foul sluttish hairs

lines.text: Which, once untangled, much misfortune bodes:
lines.plainText: Which once untangled much misfortune bodes

lines.text: This is the hag, when maids lie on their backs,
lines.plainText: This is the hag when maids lie on their backs

lines.text: That presses them, and learns them first to bear,
lines.plainText: That presses them and learns them first to bear

lines.text: Making them women of good carriage:
lines.plainText: Making them women of good carriage

lines.text: This is she,—
lines.plainText: This is she

lines.text: Peace, peace, Mercutio, peace,
lines.plainText: Peace peace Mercutio peace

lines.text: Thou talk'st of nothing.
lines.plainText: Thou talk'st of nothing

lines.text: True, I talk of dreams,
lines.plainText: True I talk of dreams

lines.text: Which are the children of an idle brain,
lines.plainText: Which are the children of an idle brain

lines.text: Begot of nothing but vain fantasy,
lines.plainText: Begot of nothing but vain fantasy

lines.text: Which is as thin of substance as the air,
lines.plainText: Which is as thin of substance as the air

lines.text: And more inconstant than the wind, who woos
lines.plainText: And more inconstant than the wind who woos

lines.text: Even now the frozen bosom of the north,
lines.plainText: Even now the frozen bosom of the north

lines.text: And, being anger'd, puffs away from thence,
lines.plainText: And being anger'd puffs away from thence

lines.text: Turning his side to the dew-dropping south.
lines.plainText: Turning his side to the dewdropping south

lines.text: This wind you talk of blows us from ourselves:
lines.plainText: This wind you talk of blows us from ourselves

lines.text: Supper is done, and we shall come too late.
lines.plainText: Supper is done and we shall come too late

lines.text: I fear too early: for my mind misgives
lines.plainText: I fear too early for my mind misgives

lines.text: Some consequence yet hanging in the stars,
lines.plainText: Some consequence yet hanging in the stars

lines.text: Shall bitterly begin his fearful date
lines.plainText: Shall bitterly begin his fearful date

lines.text: With this night's revels; and expire the term
lines.plainText: With this night's revels and expire the term

lines.text: Of a despised life, clos'd in my breast
lines.plainText: Of a despised life clos'd in my breast

lines.text: By some vile forfeit of untimely death.
lines.plainText: By some vile forfeit of untimely death

lines.text: But he that hath the steerage of my course
lines.plainText: But he that hath the steerage of my course

lines.text: Direct my suit. On, lusty gentlemen!
lines.plainText: Direct my suit On lusty gentlemen

lines.text: Strike, drum.
lines.plainText: Strike drum
